storyList.story: - She understands the design of the department store as an act of tailoring. Her form appears to be an extension of that understanding. - Using her managerial rights within the Sisyphe System, she appears capable of redefining—no, she redefines the terms of combat into something fundamentally absurd. - Recognizing and keeping to the basic tempo of the waltz produces favorable effects. - The waltz can be inferred to originate from a particular experience and desire of Jeanne’s—no, it is rooted in that particular experience and desire. - More specifically… … Our first anniversary. We had taken a table at Café de Flore, waiting for our dinner reservation—looking out, as we often did, upon the same scenery that remained unfamiliar. At some point, my attention settled on Jeanne’s hand. Her fingers were tapping along to the faint clatter of a typewriter audible beneath the noise of the café. By coincidence, its rhythm was close to that of her favorite waltz. Though Jeanne seemed somewhat absent-minded for those few moments, she did not appear dizzy. When it was time to leave, we moved to the Pont Royal. Jeanne excused herself from the table for a short while. When she was out of sight, I asked the bartender to blend that same waltz into the Experience Wine. Jeanne returned and took a sip, which seemed to noticeably improve her facial expression for as long as the aftertaste lingered. … She appeared happy. Though we’ve danced together many times before, we did so by sharing Canned Experiences of waltz dancers. We have never truly waltzed together. The first time we made plans to do so, I was unexpectedly assigned extra shifts, forcing a rain check. On our next appointed date, Jeanne couldn’t make it—the Liquidation schedule for the Grand Magasin Sisyphe had suddenly been moved up. Afterward, events both small and large continued to foil our attempts to find that sufficiently uneventful day where nothing could get in our way, and our appointment was repeatedly pushed back… Until eventually, our last appointment led us not to waltzing on the dance floor at some club, but to taking the floor at the N Corp. courthouse for my trial. … She appeared saddened. Just now, for the first time, I matched my steps to hers. I could see yearning in her eyes and voice— the yearning for me, for someone who could understand her and dance to her rhythm. But at the same time, I understood that not all of her waking moments were filled with that yearning. Moments when we’d step on each other’s toes, when she’d give a sudden tug and pull me tripping into her, when I barely managed to catch her as she leaned so deeply into me that she almost fell, when I’d noticed that the beads of sweat rolling down our foreheads had not had the chance to dry… Not a single step of our dance followed any known forms of proper dance techniques, but in the continuity of that undefined mess, the rest of the world fell away, leaving only Jeanne and me to exist. For a moment, we both forgot about things like the Golden Bough or the Grand Magasin. … She appeared to be enjoying it. For the briefest moment, she met my gaze, and I hers. I saw something in that gaze, but it was complicated—disappointment through the haze, longing, or perhaps a mix of affection and resentment. I realized that I could not assign a single name to what she was feeling. But through the smallest crack in the layers upon layers of emotions that had coated her heart, I could sense it: her anticipation, her expectation for the moment that would one day allow her to forget she was ever nauseous. And because of that… … Jeanne was enjoying this moment. That dizziness and nausea will probably never leave Jeanne. On the day she sipped Experience Wine blended with the experience of waltzing, On rainy days, And even on the coming days when the same faintness, that alienation, would take her… Jeanne felt, feels, and will feel the same surge of nausea. Despite that, with the anticipation for the briefest moment that the future holds, let me say… … I hope you enjoyed the waltz, ma lionne.
